consensus: All models used white background (#ffffff) and 1920×1080 canvas—standard for consulting decks
All placed title at top-left (x=120, y=120±0)—standard consulting anchor point
All used quarterly timeline (Q1–Q4) as temporal axis—appropriate strategic planning granularity
All rendered Gantt bars as horizontal rectangles with consistent height (40px)—visual clarity
All showed 5 workstreams/phases in vertical swim lanes—digestible executive scope
All included source citation at bottom—consulting attribution standard
All employed restrained color palette (grays + single accent color)—professional and focus-directing
All left-aligned workstream labels at x=120–140—scanability and hierarchy
All kept element count under 40—avoided visual clutter (Claude 23, Gemini 29, GPT-5 35)
contradictions: Grid structure: Claude and Gemini used vertical quarter dividers only; GPT-5 Mini added full horizontal grid lines creating a table aesthetic—tradeoff between clarity (GPT-5) and minimalism (Claude/Gemini)

Title specificity: Claude ('Enterprise Platform Build: Critical path on track') and Gemini ('ERP Modernization: Systems Integration Critical Path') communicated clear message; GPT-5 Mini ('Strategic Roadmap—FY Gantt') was generic and non-actionable
Critical path emphasis: Claude and Gemini used blue (#1971c2) for critical item; GPT-5 Mini used green (#2d6a4f) labeled 'Priority'—different semantic framing (risk vs importance)
Quarter header placement: Claude/Gemini positioned Q labels at y≈240–252 (closer to data); GPT-5 Mini at y=160 (larger gap)—affects visual grouping
Typography hierarchy: Claude used largest title (60px) then 32px headers; GPT-5 Mini and Gemini used 56px/28px—Claude's contrast stronger
Bar color semantics: Claude/Gemini kept completed work in neutral gray; GPT-5 Mini varied grays (#6c757d vs #adb5bd) suggesting two states without explicit legend
Annotation method: Claude used inline ⚠ emoji; Gemini used separate callout text box; GPT-5 Mini used bottom legend—different executive scanning patterns
partial_coverage: Only Claude included warning indicator (⚠) directly on risky workstream label—immediate risk signaling
Only GPT-5 Mini provided explicit legend/key explaining color coding—self-documenting for stakeholders unfamiliar with context
Only Gemini added background rectangles for quarter headers (300×50px boxes)—strengthened temporal axis as visual anchor
Only GPT-5 Mini included text labels ON the Gantt bars themselves ('Design & Setup', 'Platform Development')—improved scannability without cross-referencing
Only Gemini included explicit milestone callout ('Q3 Go/No-Go Gate' at decision point)—surfaced critical decision moment
Only Claude positioned 'Go/No-Go' label at x=1510, y=547 (mid-timeline)—suggests decision timing, but lacks visual connector
unique_insights: Claude: Achieved highest signal-to-noise ratio (23 elements) while maintaining clarity—demonstrates ruthless simplification principle
GPT-5 Mini: Full grid structure + on-bar labels + legend = most self-contained for distributed review (email/print scenario)—optimized for asynchronous consumption
Gemini: Quarter header backgrounds create strongest temporal scaffolding—visual hierarchy guides eye left-to-right through phases
GPT-5 Mini: Horizontal row separators (y=320, 400, 480, 560) improve swim-lane differentiation when projecting on low-contrast screens
Claude: Single blue bar (#1971c2) creates immediate focal point on critical path—efficient executive attention direction
Gemini: Consistent 300px quarter widths (600/900/1200/1500) create metronomic rhythm—aids estimation of relative durations
blind_spots: NO MODEL showed task dependencies or critical-path arrows—essential for understanding sequencing and bottleneck analysis
NO MODEL included progress indicators (actual vs planned position, % complete shading, or baseline comparison)—unable to answer 'are we on track?'
NO MODEL used diamond shapes or vertical markers for milestones—relied on text annotations instead of universal Gantt symbols
NO MODEL included 'today' or 'now' vertical line—audience cannot orient to current status without mental calculation
NO MODEL showed resource allocation, owners, or accountability—missing 'who' dimension critical for governance
NO MODEL provided quantitative metrics (budget, FTE, deliverable count)—purely temporal view lacks ROI context
NO MODEL placed legend in top-right corner—consulting standard is top-right for immediate context, not bottom or absent
NO MODEL included synthesis insight box or 'so what' callout—chart requires executive to infer implications rather than stating them
NO MODEL showed date precision beyond quarters—3-month granularity too coarse for near-term execution tracking (next 30-60 days unclear)
NO MODEL used RAG (Red/Amber/Green) status indicators on workstreams—binary 'warning emoji' (Claude) insufficient for nuanced risk portfolio
NO MODEL distinguished workstream labels from bar labels typographically—could use bolder/larger treatment for swimlane headers vs activity names
NO MODEL included phase gates or governance checkpoints visually—'Go/No-Go' mentioned but not rendered as decision diamond or stage-gate marker
ALL MODELS positioned source at bottom—consulting best practice is top-right in smaller font (12–14pt) to preserve content real estate
